scope: Frozen V1 training sources, saved architecture metadata, HDF5 labels only, original training logs, permitted RC diagnostic provenance, and official BioWulf resource documentation. No external benchmark outcome table was opened by this audit.

phase_one.hash_evidence: Both original training_manifest.tsv files and COPD-V2-RC_scoring_manifest.json; original scripts were independently hashed during this audit, model weights were not rehashed here.
phase_one.sequence_ambiguity_policy: Uppercase sequence; A/C/G/T one-hot; every other symbol becomes an all-zero row. V1 did not exclude N-containing sequences.
phase_one.sequence_window_rule: For BED [start,end), retrieve [start-501,end+500), exactly 2001 bp. Do not silently replace this with a different summit-centered window.
phase_one.representation: Final 4560-dimensional sigmoid output of the complete frozen phase-I model, not a hidden layer and not a nucleotide-axis embedding.
phase_one.frozen_inference_mode_requirement: Load exact weights; fail hard if absent/hash mismatch. Set training=False to disable dropout; phase I is never optimized in V2. Original code merely warned and continued with random weights if missing, which must not be retained as permissible behavior.

phase_two.trainable_kernel_initializer: GlorotUniform controlled by fixed global training seed
phase_two.saved_metadata_check: Read config.json inside each original phase_two_model.keras ZIP without importing TensorFlow; saved layer defaults and optimizer agree between models.

historical_weights.note: These historical V1 checkpoints remain immutable and are not V2 initializations selected using outcomes. New V2 phase-II models are independently initialized using each prespecified seed.

original_training.class_weighting: None; each retained region is one training example.
original_training.checkpoint_rule: Save best validation loss; minimum val_loss, mode auto/min; restore best weights; early stopping patience 15, default min_delta 0, no baseline.
original_training.device: One NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB. GPUS=4 in code multiplies batch size only; multi-GPU wrapper is commented out.

builder_equivalence_evidence.limitation: Ten-sequence equivalence check, not an all-example equivalence test.

frozen_training_inputs.BED_to_HDF5_count_check: All six class-by-split counts in both stored HDF5 datasets match the original BED partition table exactly; zero sequence exclusions detected by count reconciliation. Labels were read directly without reading embedding arrays.
frozen_training_inputs.sequence_exclusion: Only absent chromosome or non-2001-bp extracted sequence; streaming implementation also explicitly rejects negative start. No N/ambiguity exclusion.
frozen_training_inputs.control_construction: External pre-windowed pan-source DHS controls, not required to overlap this donor ATAC. Exclude relevant mark, blacklist, TSS +/-2000bp promoters, and positive 1000bp windows; globally sample without replacement to total ratio 2:1 using seed 20261001. Per-chromosome ratios are not fixed 2:1. Mark/blacklist/promoter exclusion was applied to 1000bp core windows, not full 2001bp flanks.
frozen_training_inputs.source_combination: All donor lobes concatenated and exact full narrowPeak rows deduplicated separately per mark; ATAC-peak versus histone overlap then occurs across these unions. Positive windows are deduplicated by chromosome and start, but nearby overlapping windows remain distinct.
frozen_training_inputs.genomic_or_sequence_duplicate_partition_: Not determined by this architecture audit; full interval/sequence construction QC must check core and expanded-window identity, RC-canonical sequence identity and partition membership. Do not assert duplicate safety solely from chromosome names.

historical_region_threshold_leakage.finding: V1 computes roc_curve(Y_test,Y_pred) on chr8-9, then selects threshold nearest target FPR and saves it for candidate scoring. This is explicitly test-derived calibration, not validation-derived.

historical_delta_rule.finding: Absolute ALT-REF >=95th percentile among eligible candidate-universe scores, separately by model and SNV versus indel/complex; not experimentally calibrated allele-effect evidence.

rc_diagnostic_justification.finding: Score orientation sensitivity is scientifically material for both models under the prespecified RC audit; this independently justifies orientation correction without consulting external benchmark outcomes.

leakage_and_orientation_findings.augmentation_recommendation: Cache g(sequence) and g(RC(sequence)) using frozen phase I; never reverse a 4560-dimensional embedding. Draw one orientation per biological region per epoch with prespecified seeded Bernoulli(0.5), preserving per-region weight and V1 steps per epoch. If instead both views are used each epoch, predeclare half-weights and increased compute; do not silently double training exposure.
leakage_and_orientation_findings.inference_recommendation: For each seed average phase-II probabilities h(g(sequence)) and h(g(RC(sequence))) with weight 1/2, then average all three seeds with weight 1/3. Do not average phase-I embeddings before nonlinear phase II. Disable dropout and use inference-mode BatchNorm. REF and ALT are independently symmetrized.
leakage_and_orientation_findings.mathematical_invariance: With R(R(s))=s, p_sym(R(s))=[f(R(s))+f(s)]/2=p_sym(s); averaging the same three seed-level p_sym preserves this identity. Nonfinite outputs or failures beyond prespecified floating-point tolerance are hard QC failures.
leakage_and_orientation_findings.checkpoint_recommendation: Preserve minimum validation BCE, max 50 epochs and patience 15, but compute validation BCE on the symmetric inference probabilities to select the deployed predictor. Treat this as an explicitly prespecified orientation-handling adaptation, not external-outcome-guided model selection.

historical_resource_evidence.timing_limitations: Epoch seconds are rounded log-reported training-plus-validation timing, not scheduler accounting. Dataset and log mtimes supply approximate extraction/whole-run elapsed evidence only; they include initialization/I/O and are not separately instrumented phase-I timings. No original MaxRSS or sacct resource-allocation record was located. Both models ran all 50 epochs, not approximately 16. Frozen phase-I pretraining cost is sunk and is not repeated.

prospective_compute_plan.run_matrix: 3 staged configurations x 2 region-label models x 3 prespecified seeds = 18 new phase-II fits, plus shared frozen phase-I dual-orientation feature extraction. Frozen V1 requires zero retraining.
prospective_compute_plan.GPU_type: A100 80GB to match observed V1 hardware; use one GPU per fit, not four.
prospective_compute_plan.feature_extraction: After separate investigator approval only: extract each unique frozen 2001bp sequence in each orientation once; cache by sequence/weights/build hash and share read-only across all seeds/configurations. Do not compute or reveal test metrics until the selected configuration and calibration are frozen.
prospective_compute_plan.phase_two_projection_formula_seconds: For each model/configuration: historical 50-epoch fit seconds * (new train examples / historical train examples), then multiply by 3 seeds. This is an approximate scaling model, not an executed performance result. Add symmetric-validation and I/O overhead.
prospective_compute_plan.reference_size_assumption: Every A/B/C dataset has the V1 training size; one orientation sample per region per epoch; 50 epochs each. Revised interval counts may lower or raise this estimate; use actual frozen counts in final preflight.
prospective_compute_plan.requested_capacity_vs_expected_cost: 18 four-hour fit limits plus one four-hour cache limit permit up to 76 GPU-hours but do not predict consumption. 12-24 GPU-hours is a conservative planning budget before actual final counts/throughput. Queue waiting is excluded and unpredictable.
prospective_compute_plan.host_memory_design: Stream HDF5 blocks; never materialize all sequence one-hot arrays or both orientation feature sets for all configurations simultaneously. 48 GB host memory is a planning allocation, not measured MaxRSS.
prospective_compute_plan.cache_storage_formula_bytes: unique_sequence_count * 2 orientations * 4560 float32 values * 4 bytes = 36480 * N, before compression and metadata.
prospective_compute_plan.cache_bound_assumption: 3 x (544056 + 91752) examples with no cross-model or cross-configuration deduplication and both orientations. Actual unique cache should be smaller if frozen counts do not exceed V1.
prospective_compute_plan.checkpoint_storage: Approximately 334 MiB each saved Keras model and weight checkpoint in V1; archiving both for 18 fits is approximately 12 GiB, plus histories/manifests. Keep only prescribed best checkpoint and final metadata, not every epoch unless separately budgeted.
prospective_compute_plan.CPU_data_audit_estimate: Separate CPU-only construction/QC: plan 8 CPUs, 32-64 GB RAM, 1-4 hours (8-32 allocated CPU-hours), with actual measured usage to supersede estimate. Source sequence I/O and pairwise matching dominate uncertainty.
prospective_compute_plan.parallelization: Feature extraction can be sharded deterministically by disjoint chromosome/sequence-key ranges with atomic per-shard outputs. Freeze and verify cache before training consumers. The 18 fits are independent after data/cache freeze; cap concurrent one-GPU fits at 4 initially to limit filesystem pressure. Do not let array completion order influence checkpoint/configuration choice.
prospective_compute_plan.conditional_bootstrap_runtime: Validation block-bootstrap and summaries are CPU-only and can be parallelized by prespecified replicate index without changing seed aggregation. Exact runtime depends on fixed replicate count and frozen validation sample counts.
prospective_compute_plan.uncertainty: No GPU pilot was run. Accessible-control counts, same-lobe filtering, storage contention, caching implementation, and symmetric validation may alter runtime. These are estimates, not measured V2 runtimes.

BioWulf_current_read_only_checks.planning_implication: 8 CPUs and 48 GB host memory per single-A100 job fit within one quarter of an A100 node. Official documentation limits CPUs per allocated GPU to node CPUs divided by node GPUs (16 on this type). Use batchlim/freen again only when the investigator authorizes scheduling, because limits/availability can change.

sources.supports: GPU partition and --gres request syntax; CPU-per-GPU limit; batchlim for up-to-date walltime/resource limits.
Public A100 hardware: 80 GB VRAM, four GPUs and 64 CPUs per node.
freen and batchlim read-only resource inspection.
